plot: Odo and Mothwick wait on Robbins Pond Road for the real Paulding Light (Michigan, since 1966); legends say a brakeman's lantern, Michigan Tech's 2010 telescope shows headlights on US-45 — then a light leaves the road and drifts toward Odo.

script.title: Since 1966, This Light Comes Back Every Night

beats.say: A true story. Since nineteen sixty-six, in a valley near Paulding, Michigan, a light has come back almost every night.
Mothwick... why did we stop at the end of a dirt road?
This is Robbins Pond Road. People drive here after dark. They park. They wait.
Wait for what?
For the light. Look down the valley, along the power lines.
In nineteen sixty-six, teenagers reported it to the sheriff. A glowing ball, far down the valley.
It brightens. It fades. Some nights it seems to change colour. Then it simply goes out.
It went out. Is it gone?
No. It always comes back. That's the part people never forget.
Locals call it the Paulding Light, or the Dog Meadow Light. And they say someone carries it.
The most famous story says it is a lantern, held by a railroad brakeman.
Stop the train! There are cars stopped on the track!
The legend says he died trying to warn a train, swinging his lantern in the dark.
And they say he never stopped swinging it.
He's still waiting for the train...
Others tell it differently. The ghost of a mail carrier who never finished his route.
Another tells of a grandparent searching for a lost grandchild, relighting a lantern again and again.
That, they say, is why the light comes and goes.
Then I understand him. I carry a lantern too.
Keep it lit, little one. Whatever you see tonight.
For decades, the light kept coming. Nobody could explain it.
In two thousand ten, students from Michigan Tech carried a telescope to the viewing spot.
Watch closely, Odo. Science is about to spoil a perfectly good ghost story.
Through the lens, the floating glow had a shape. Two lights. Side by side. Moving.
Two lights... like eyes?
Like headlights. Cars on Highway forty-five, about five miles to the north.
Then they drove a car along that highway. The Paulding Light appeared, right on cue.
High beams made it brighter. Police flashers made it shimmer in colours.
Investigators said the same in nineteen ninety. Headlights and taillights.
So there's no brakeman. No lantern. Just cars.
That is what the telescope says.
And yet people still come. The Forest Service even put up a sign about the light.
Because when that light rises over the silent valley, nobody is thinking about cars.
Mothwick... the light is coming toward us.
Headlights don't leave the road, Odo.
Then what is that?

long.title: Since 1966, This Light Comes Back Every Night 🏮
long.description:
A true story from Michigan's Upper Peninsula: since 1966 a glowing light has risen over a valley near Paulding almost every night. Legend says it is a dead brakeman's lantern — in 2010 a telescope found another answer. Would you wait on Robbins Pond Road after dark?
